newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S. dollar rise could help EU single currency.
newsitem.headline: U.S. dollar rise could help EU single currency.

text.p: The rise of the U.S. dollar against the German mark and other currencies could help the European Union meet its single currency goals, the EU's monetary affairs commissioner suggested on Tuesday.
Yves-Thibault de Silguy told a European Parliament hearing that the recent appreciation of the U.S. currency could boost the 15-nation bloc's growth this year.
He was hesitant, however, about predicting the effect of any greater rise.
De Silguy said that recent studies of the state of the EU's overall economy confirmed a prediction made by the European Commission in autumn that bloc-wide growth was set to be about 2.3 percent.
But that could be boosted by the current strong dollar, which would lower the costs of EU products on world markets and increase the cost of U.S. exports.
"We note that the appreciation of the dollar -- more than 10 percent above the average for 1996 -- constitutes a positive factor which could lead to raising (the growth estimate)," de Silguy said.
Dollar to mark rates of the like seen earlier in February would add significantly to the bloc's Gross Domestic Product.
"With the dollar at 1.75 deutschemarks, that is around 0.3 to 0.4 percent (of GDP growth) over three or four quarters," he said.
But it was unclear what effect a much higher dollar would have. "At 1.90 or 1.92 marks, nobody knows what the effect would be," he said.
The dollar was trading at about 1.67 to the mark on Tuesday.
Although de Silguy did not make the direct link, any rise in GDP would make it easier for EU countries to meet the qualifying criteria for the single European currency, the euro.
Countries are to be judged on whether they have met the criteria early next year, based on their economic performance this year.
One key criterion is for countries to have a public deficit to GDP ratio of no more than three percent. A rising GDP would lower the ratio.
De Silguy said he was already happy with the efforts made by EU countries to get their budgets in order for the euro, a process he said was already bearing fruit.
